      eBird region codes, explained

      What is an eBird region code?

      An eBird region code identifies a geographic area in eBird's system, for example US-NC-119 for Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, or GB-ENG for England. eBird regions go from country to state/province to county.

      How do I find my eBird region code?

      Type your town into the search box above. The finder matches it to its region and shows the eBird region code, which you can copy or open directly on eBird.org.

      Can I use eBird region codes with the eBird API?

      Yes. Plug the code into eBird API endpoints such as https://api.ebird.org/v2/data/obs/US-NC-119/recent to pull recent bird observations for that county. You need a free eBird API key, available at ebird.org/api/keygen.

      Why does my town show a neighboring county's code?

      Some towns sit on county lines. The finder uses each town's primary county, which is the county eBird associates with most checklists there.

      Can I see recent bird sightings near me?

      Yes. Pick a town in the finder above, then enter your free eBird API key in the Birds Near Me section. Recent sightings near that town load automatically.
